_readme: Pins for tools/gen_rr_{species,types,natdex,encounters,sprites,priority_trainers}.py (docs/gen3_requirements.md F-7). Each generator fetches its named source through tools/fetch_rr_sources.py:cached_source(), which verifies the sha256 before returning bytes -- a mismatch is a hard failure, never a silent pass. Populate the cache with `python tools/fetch_rr_sources.py --fetch` (writes to $SLINK_RR_SRC_CACHE, default data/.rr_src_cache/).

funnotbun_species_h.note: funnotbun/funnotbun.github.io no longer exists on GitHub (confirmed 404 via `gh api repos/funnotbun/funnotbun.github.io` and `git ls-remote` on 2026-09-26); the generator's live main-branch fetch can never succeed again. Pinned to a Wayback Machine capture instead. The CDX index shows this file byte-identical (digest YUYPPBYEOOJCVQKELVW5CAKXCTCT4IK2) across every capture from 2023-09-03 through 2026-04-22, so the content predates and survives the repo's deletion -- a stable pin, not a moving one.

funnotbun_base_stats_c.note: Same dead repo as funnotbun_species_h. CDX digest GW4OJ6VZ2IG4S7ABEFPHE3U4E5TOSMSC is identical across every capture 2023-09-03..2025-07-30.

funnotbun_wild_encounter_tables_c.note: Same dead repo. CDX digest 3PCAWEJB24UWK4WVP3PCJ3KB3DPEP5V5 identical across every capture 2023-10-12..2026-04-22 -- the newest capture available (2026-04-22, months after the live repo's deletion) still matches, confirming the archive is a faithful, unchanging pin.

jwowsquared_data_js.note: gen_rr_sprites.py already vendors from this repo (the funnotbun sprite source is gone too) but read the moving 'master' ref live. Pinned to master's HEAD commit as of 2026-09-26 (`git ls-remote https://github.com/JwowSquared/Radical-Red-Pokedex.git refs/heads/master`).

rr_priority_trainers_sheet_xlsx.note: Community Google Sheet, no immutable revision URL -- this pins today's (2026-09-26) content snapshot only. NOT a raw-file sha256: two exports of this URL fetched minutes apart, with no sheet edit in between, produced different zip bytes every time (Google's xlsx exporter reorders/rewrites xl/sharedStrings.xml and xl/worksheets/*.xml non-deterministically on every export -- confirmed by unzipping both and diffing). content_sha256 instead hashes openpyxl's (sheet, row, col, repr(value)) cell tuples with data_only=True, which WAS identical across both test fetches. It deliberately excludes the data_only=False formula view (used only for `=IMAGE(...)` trainer-sprite URLs) because that view was NOT stable across the same two fetches either -- ponytail: sprite_url is cosmetic, not worth chasing a stable hash for. A later --fetch will FAIL content_sha256 verification once the community sheet is next edited; that is the pin doing its job. Re-pin deliberately: fetch, diff the parsed roster against the committed one, and only then update this hash.
